def-variational-autoencoder:
## Definition

Let $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A_X,\mu_X)$ and $(\mathcal Z,\mathcal A_Z,\mu_Z)$ be sigma-finite measure spaces; that is, each has a countable measurable cover by sets of finite measure. Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_\theta}$ and $\Phi\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_\phi}$ be parameter sets of finite dimension. A latent-variable model with parameter $\theta\in\Theta$ consists of a measurable prior density $r_\theta(z)\ge0$ on $\mathcal Z$ and a decoder density $d_\theta(x\mid z)\ge0$ on $\mathcal X$ for each $z$, with
$$\int_{\mathcal Z} r_\theta(z)\,d\mu_Z(z)=1,\qquad \int_{\mathcal X} d_\theta(x\mid z)\,d\mu_X(x)=1.$$
The decoder is jointly measurable in $(x,z)$, and the joint model density is
$$p_\theta(x,z)=\gamma_\theta(z;x):=r_\theta(z)d_\theta(x\mid z)$$
relative to $\mu_X\otimes\mu_Z$. The decoder is also called the generative model: after drawing $z$ from the prior, it assigns a conditional density to the observation $x$.

For a fixed observation $x$, the evidence density and posterior density are
$$Z_\theta(x):=p_\theta(x):=\int_{\mathcal Z}\gamma_\theta(z;x)\,d\mu_Z(z),\qquad \pi_\theta(z\mid x):=\frac{\gamma_\theta(z;x)}{Z_\theta(x)}.$$
Use this posterior only when $0<Z_\theta(x)<\infty$. A variational encoder is a jointly measurable family of functions $q_\phi(z\mid x)\ge0$ on $\mathcal Z$, parameterized by $\phi\in\Phi$ and normalized by
$$\int_{\mathcal Z}q_\phi(z\mid x)\,d\mu_Z(z)=1$$
for every $(\phi,x)$; the same parameter $\phi$ is used for each observation. For an admissible triple $(\theta,\phi,x)$ require
$$q_\phi(z\mid x)=0\quad\mu_Z\text{-almost everywhere on }\{z:\pi_\theta(z\mid x)=0\},\qquad \int_{\mathcal Z}q_\phi(z\mid x)\bigl(|\log\gamma_\theta(z;x)|+|\log q_\phi(z\mid x)|\bigr)\,d\mu_Z(z)<\infty.$$
Terms multiplied by $q_\phi=0$ are defined to be zero. The evidence lower bound is
$$\operatorname{ELBO}_{\theta,\phi}(x):=\int_{\mathcal Z}q_\phi(z\mid x)\bigl(\log\gamma_\theta(z;x)-\log q_\phi(z\mid x)\bigr)\,d\mu_Z(z).$$

A pathwise representation of the encoder at $x$ is a probability space $(\mathcal E,\mathcal F,\rho)$ whose law $\rho$ is independent of $\theta$ and $\phi$, together with a measurable map $g_\phi(\epsilon,x)$ such that the law of $g_\phi(\epsilon,x)$ for $\epsilon\sim\rho$ is the measure with density $q_\phi(\cdot\mid x)$ relative to $\mu_Z$. This representation defines how to generate encoder samples; it does not by itself assert that differentiation may pass through an expectation.
cor-vae-elbo-kl-decomposition:
## Statement

Fix an observation $x$ in a VAE with latent reference measure $\mu_Z$. Let $\gamma_\theta(\cdot;x)$ be its nonnegative measurable joint-density slice, let $Z_\theta(x)=\int\gamma_\theta(z;x)\,d\mu_Z(z)\in(0,\infty)$, and let $\pi_\theta(z\mid x)=\gamma_\theta(z;x)/Z_\theta(x)$. Let $q_\phi(\cdot\mid x)$ be a measurable probability density satisfying $q_\phi=0$ $\mu_Z$-almost everywhere on $\{\pi_\theta=0\}$ and
$$\int q_\phi(z\mid x)\bigl(|\log\gamma_\theta(z;x)|+|\log q_\phi(z\mid x)|\bigr)\,d\mu_Z(z)<\infty.$$
Then the choice-free density-ratio identity is
$$\log Z_\theta(x)=\operatorname{ELBO}_{\theta,\phi}(x)+\int q_\phi(z\mid x)\log\!\left(\frac{q_\phi(z\mid x)}{\pi_\theta(z\mid x)}\right)\,d\mu_Z(z),$$
where the ratio integrand is zero when $q_\phi=0$. Under the Axiom of Choice, the final integral is the library reverse-KL divergence $D_{\rm KL}(q_\phi\mu_Z\|\pi_\theta\mu_Z)$ and is nonnegative; hence $\operatorname{ELBO}_{\theta,\phi}(x)\le\log Z_\theta(x)$.
thm-reparameterization-gradient-under-do:
## Statement

Let $X=(x_1,\ldots,x_N)$ be a fixed nonempty finite data set, let $\Lambda$ be an open subset of a finite-dimensional Euclidean parameter space for $\eta=(\theta,\phi)$, and fix $\eta_0=(\theta_0,\phi_0)\in\Lambda$. For each $i$, assume the VAE at $(\eta,x_i)$ is admissible and has a pathwise representation $g_\phi(\epsilon,x_i)$ under one parameter-independent probability law $\rho$. Assume there is one $\rho$-null set, common to every $i$ and $\eta\in\Lambda$, outside which $0<q_\phi(g_\phi(\epsilon,x_i)\mid x_i)<\infty$ and $0<\gamma_\theta(g_\phi(\epsilon,x_i);x_i)<\infty$; define the payoff below to be zero on that null set. Define
$$H_i(\eta,\epsilon):=\log\gamma_\theta(g_\phi(\epsilon,x_i);x_i)-\log q_\phi(g_\phi(\epsilon,x_i)\mid x_i),$$
with terms on a common $\rho$-null set defined to be zero. Assume each $H_i$ is jointly measurable and integrable for every $\eta\in\Lambda$. Outside one $\rho$-null set, each $H_i(\cdot,\epsilon)$ is continuously differentiable on $\Lambda$ with continuous gradient, and $\nabla_\eta H_i(\eta,\cdot)$ is measurable for every $\eta$. For every compact neighborhood $K\subset\Lambda$ of $\eta_0$, assume one nonnegative $M_{i,K}\in L^1(\rho)$ satisfies $\|\nabla_\eta H_i(\eta,\epsilon)\|_2\le M_{i,K}(\epsilon)$ for every $\eta\in K$ outside one common null set, and assume $\mathbb E_\rho\|\nabla_\eta H_i(\eta_0,\epsilon)\|_2^2<\infty$.

Let $I$ be uniform on $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ and independent of $\epsilon\sim\rho$. Then the finite-average objective
$$\overline{\mathcal L}(\eta):=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\operatorname{ELBO}_{\theta,\phi}(x_i)$$
is differentiable at $\eta_0$, and its one-example pathwise gradient estimate
$$G(\eta_0,I,\epsilon):=\nabla_\eta H_I(\eta_0,\epsilon)$$
satisfies $\mathbb E[G(\eta_0,I,\epsilon)]=\nabla_\eta\overline{\mathcal L}(\eta_0)$ and has finite coordinate variances. A parameter-independent Gaussian base law alone does not imply the differentiability, envelope, or second-moment hypotheses.
alg-reparameterized-variational-training:
## Definition

Inputs are a fixed nonempty finite data set $X=(x_1,\ldots,x_N)$; a VAE model and admissible encoder from the preceding definition; a parameter-independent base law $\rho$ and pathwise map $g_\phi$ for every $x_i$; an initial parameter $\eta_0=(\theta_0,\phi_0)$; a finite positive integer $T$; and positive learning rates $\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{T-1}$. Require the hypotheses of the dominated pathwise-gradient theorem at every parameter value reached by the procedure, and require each update below to remain in its open admissible parameter domain.

Set $\eta_0=(\theta_0,\phi_0)$. For each $t=0,\ldots,T-1$:

1. Draw $I_t$ uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ and draw $\epsilon_t$ from $\rho$, independently of $I_t$ and of earlier random draws.
2. Set $z_t=g_{\phi_t}(\epsilon_t,x_{I_t})$ and evaluate
   $$h_t=\log\gamma_{\theta_t}(z_t;x_{I_t})-\log q_{\phi_t}(z_t\mid x_{I_t}).$$
3. Holding $\epsilon_t$ and $I_t$ fixed, compute the Euclidean gradient
   $$G_t=\nabla_{(\theta,\phi)}\bigl[\log\gamma_\theta(g_\phi(\epsilon_t,x_{I_t});x_{I_t})-\log q_\phi(g_\phi(\epsilon_t,x_{I_t})\mid x_{I_t})\bigr]\big|_{(\theta,\phi)=\eta_t}.$$
4. Update $\eta_{t+1}=\eta_t+\alpha_tG_t$.

Return $(\eta_0,\ldots,\eta_T)$ and $(h_t,G_t)_{0\le t<T}$. This finite procedure specifies stochastic ascent on the finite-average ELBO; it makes no claim that the iterates converge or reach a global maximum.
